context:
Work in phases, each independently testable and committable:

Phase 1 (w1-w2): Extract shared infrastructure for the primitives fork. These are the
highest-value targets with byte-for-byte identical code. Create new shared modules,
update imports, verify with existing tests.

Phase 2 (w3-w5): Consolidate benchmark base class methods and query infrastructure.
These are lower-risk refactors touching well-tested code paths.

Phase 3 (w6-w8): Minor utility extraction, ignore-list configuration, and threshold
adjustment. This is the cleanup phase.

For each consolidation:
1. Read both/all copies side-by-side to confirm true equivalence
2. Create the shared module with the canonical implementation
3. Update all call sites to use the shared version
4. Run targeted tests for affected modules
5. Run make duplicate-check-verbose to confirm line count drop
6. Commit
description:
The `make duplicate-check-verbose` tool reports 440 duplicate function groups totalling
~17,595 duplicated lines (threshold: 20,000). After careful analysis of the top 30 groups,
13 groups are genuine parallel implementations that should be consolidated, while 17 are
intended boilerplate (interface implementations, structural patterns, or facade delegations)
that should be marked for ignore.

This work reduces the duplicated-line count by an estimated 2,500-3,000 lines through
targeted consolidation of the highest-value groups, while configuring the duplicate checker
to suppress known-intentional patterns so future regressions are caught at a lower threshold.

Key consolidation targets (by estimated line savings):
- transaction_primitives/write_primitives generator fork (~530 lines)
- catalog loaders (transaction/write/metadata/read primitives) (~310 lines)
- benchmark base class (generate_data, load_data_to_database) (~210 lines)
- query manager base class (get_query, _load_queries pattern) (~140 lines)
- DataFrame query registry list_*_queries functions (~120 lines)
- platform adapter apply_constraint_configuration / apply_unified_tuning (~360 lines via ignore)

anti_patterns.dont: change public API signatures during consolidation
anti_patterns.why: downstream code and tests depend on them

anti_patterns.dont: consolidate code that only looks structurally similar
anti_patterns.instead: always read the actual implementations to confirm true duplication

anti_patterns.dont: consolidate platform adapter interface methods (from_config, apply_constraint_configuration)
anti_patterns.why: these are intended per-platform implementations even when structurally identical

anti_patterns.instead: use mixins or standalone utility functions instead
anti_patterns.why: the adapter hierarchy is already 3 levels deep

deferrals.reason: The two benchmarks share generators and catalogs but have distinct query sets and validation logic. Full unification requires deeper analysis of behavioral differences.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: transaction_primitives + write_primitives already share generators/catalogs (consolidate-duplicate-code done); full module unification of two benchmarks with intentionally distinct query sets/validation is speculative, unscoped, and the note itself hedges it needs 'deeper analysis'.

deferrals.reason: These are similar (~79 lines each) but have platform-specific error handling and cursor semantics. Consolidation requires careful testing against live platforms.
Protocol methods in protocols.py have structural duplication but serve as the interface contract. Changing them risks breaking the protocol hierarchy.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: protocols.py DataFrame protocol methods are the interface contract; structural similarity across Protocol declarations is by-design. consolidate-duplicate-code (DONE) correctly excluded them. Consolidation is inappropriate, not deferred work.
deferrals.summary: Unify DataFrame protocol abstract method definitions

load_operations_catalog() and load_query_catalog() functions.

work_units.notes:
Create a DataGenerationMixin in benchbox/core/benchmark_mixins.py (standalone,
not modifying the existing base class hierarchy):
- generate_data(): 5 copies differ only in TABLES reference.
  Mixin provides the method; each benchmark defines _get_table_schema() -> dict.
- load_data_to_database(): 3 copies (clickbench, read_primitives, ssb).
  Parameterize the schema dict and provide as mixin method.
Each benchmark class adds the mixin to its bases and implements _get_table_schema().
Estimated savings: ~210 duplicated lines.
work_units.summary: Extract common benchmark mixin with generate_data() and load_data_to_database()

- Abstract _generate_default_params(query_id)

work_units.notes:
The filtering logic in list_*_queries (family/category filter over get_all_queries)

Move this logic to QueryRegistry.list_queries(family, category) method.
Each registry file's list_*_queries becomes a one-liner delegation.
Estimated savings: ~120 duplicated lines.
work_units.summary: Add list_queries() method to QueryRegistry class, simplify 9 registry wrapper functions

work_units.notes:
After consolidation work is complete, update pyproject.toml
[tool.benchbox.duplicates] section or the check_duplicate_code.py script
to suppress known-intentional patterns:
- Platform adapter interface methods (from_config, apply_constraint_configuration,

- DataFrame adapter cast_date/cast_string implementations
- Facade/delegation one-liners

Lower the threshold from 20,000 to catch future regressions.
